subject.title: [Feature]: Expose per-run token usage on the WebSocket lifecycle event stream

question: Should OpenClaw add a public Gateway WebSocket per-run usage event, and should it be a lifecycle `phase: "usage"` payload or a separate run-status/diagnostic event contract?
rationale: Current main has usage RPCs and diagnostic model.usage events, but adding usage to the public agent WebSocket stream creates a compatibility-sensitive client contract that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve a narrow lifecycle usage contract
options.body: Define one additive event shape with runId/sessionKey/agentId/provider/model/usage/lastCallUsage/duration and require coverage across the relevant run paths before implementation lands.

options.title: Use diagnostics and RPC surfaces only
options.body: Document diagnostics model.usage and sessions.usage as the supported integration path and close the Gateway lifecycle event request as out of scope.

options.title: Fold into broader run status work
options.body: Defer this issue into a broader run-status/event-stream design so usage, status, and terminal semantics ship as one coherent contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow lifecycle usage contract
recommendation.body: Define one additive event shape with runId/sessionKey/agentId/provider/model/usage/lastCallUsage/duration and require coverage across the relevant run paths before implementation lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the public Gateway event/protocol boundary and adjacent diagnostics surface, where this account has recent history.
